title: GTA 6 Finally Ditches the Frustrating X Button Sprint
description: Recent reports reveal that GTA 6 will no longer force players to mash the X button to sprint, replacing it with the standard L3 stick press to improve controls.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## A Welcome Relief: GTA 6 Abandons the Notorious X Button Sprint

Most of the games that Rockstar Games creates are widely considered masterpieces by critics and fans alike. From intricately detailed open worlds to compelling narratives, their titles consistently set the benchmark for the entire gaming industry. However, if there is any criticism that frequently surfaces shortly after their games launch, it usually concerns the control schemes.

### The Long-Standing Control Frustration

The most notorious example of this in Rockstar’s legacy is the infamous demand to constantly mash the X button on the controller just to make your character sprint. For years, navigating the vast open worlds or escaping high-intensity pursuit missions meant subjecting your thumb to relentless, repetitive tapping. It was a tiring mechanic that many players grew to resent over the span of countless hours.

### Moving Forward with Modern Controls

According to a recent report by gaming media outlet Push Square, this classic pain point is finally being addressed in the highly anticipated *Grand Theft Auto VI*. The update reveals a much-needed quality-of-life change: now, you simply press L3 to run.

While it may seem like a minor adjustment to outsiders, transitioning to the L3 button brings Rockstar's control layout in line with modern gaming standards. It eliminates unnecessary physical strain during long play sessions and allows players to focus entirely on immersing themselves in the game's expansive world without fighting their controllers.

## Editor's Take

Rockstar has always done things its own way, but stubbornly sticking to outdated control quirks has sometimes hindered the experience. Adopting the L3 sprint for *GTA 6* shows a pragmatic willingness to listen to players. It's a small change on paper, but a massive win for overall comfort and playability.
